title: Causal segment reassembly and customer escalation runbook for hosted SSE partial outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Several customers using the Hosted API over SSE observed partial output sequences (truncated tokens and out-of-order segments) after mid-stream disconnects. Unlike earlier incidents that focused on reconnect heuristics, these reports point to a subtle causal reassembly bug in the server-side segmenting logic that can interleave KV cache boundaries and produce missing or duplicated tokens when a reconnect occurs during a flush window. This ticket coordinates immediate mitigations, customer comms, and the longer-term fix and rollout plan.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create a long streaming generation (>= 3k tokens) using a model variant that triggers KV cache flush policy (frequent attention recompute). 2) Force a mid-stream network interruption from the client side after a chunk boundary but before KV commit (simulate intermittent edge proxy behavior). 3) Reconnect and resume streaming via client resume token/state. 4) Observe: final output contains repeated phrases in the middle and a missing sentence after the reconnect point in ~3% of runs under heavy load; higher with batching enabled.
investigation_summary: Root cause (current hypothesis): A race between the segment-commit path and the session-snapshot operation leads to inconsistent segment sequence numbers being returned to the resume path. Specifically, when the server is under sustained batching pressure, an edge flush compacts multiple in-flight frames; the session snapshot used for resume can contain an older segment base index which causes the reassembly step to apply a wrong offset. This produces both duplicated tokens (when a previously sent segment is re-applied) and dropped tokens (when the resume offset skips a pending segment). Differences across Hosted/Dedicated/Private: Dedicated and Private deployments with tuned KV flush intervals show lower incidence, suggesting timing/throughput dependence rather than model-specific behavior.
temporary_mitigations:
- Server-side fast patch: add a verification check when applying resume offsets: validate sequence monotonicity and fall back to conservative full session resend path if mismatch detected (feature-flagged).
- Short-term config: disable aggressive compacting during customer sessions flagged as at-risk (config toggle per-tenant).
- Customer comms: notify impacted customers with temporary guidance: (1) avoid mid-generation disconnects, (2) use shorter max_stream_chunk_size as workaround.
- Support playbook: for escalations, collect session IDs, server logs (session-snapshot, segment-commit timestamps), and client resume tokens.
long_term_fix:
1) Rework resume protocol: include stable session epoch + checksum per segment so resume applies deterministic reassembly (add a 64-bit segment checksum and epoch number to snapshot).
2) Move commit ordering to a single writer barrier to eliminate race (introduce lightweight sequence coordinator piggybacked on existing request path).
3) Add integration tests that simulate edge-proxy disconnect patterns and heavy batching to detect regressions.
4) Backfill a compatibility shim for older snapshots where epoch/checksum absent.
5) Performance validation: ensure new barrier doesn't increase p99 latency by more than 5% under baseline workloads.
rollout_plan:
- Stage 1 (hotfix): deploy verification check behind a feature flag to Hosted canary (5% tenants) -> monitor error rate and customer reports for 72hrs.
- Stage 2 (config): enable conservative compacting for flagged tenants while we develop the protocol change.
- Stage 3 (protocol change): land epoch+checksum change with backward-compatible shim; ship to Dedicated first (closed tenants) then to Hosted canary 10% then full.
- Stage 4: enable new sequence coordinator and retire shim after 4 weeks of stable telemetry.
- Rollback criteria: increase in stream-failure rates > 0.5% above baseline or p99 token latency regression > 5%.
qa_test_plan:
- Unit: new checksum calculation and epoch encoding tests.
- Integration: chaos tests that inject disconnects at randomized offsets across 50k simulated sessions.
- E2E: run against models with long-context (>= 8k) with both batching on and off; validate byte-for-byte equivalence of resumed and uninterrupted runs (modulo expected timing differences).
- Performance: stress test to measure p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput with coordinator enabled.
- Canary validation queries: define 30 representative prompts (conversational, long-form, code generation) and run 1k iterations during canary to verify semantic fidelity.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- New metric: resume_sequence_mismatch_count (tagged by tenant, model, backend-host).
- Alert: fire P1 when resume_sequence_mismatch_count > 5 for any tenant in 1h.
- Dashboard: per-tenant streaming integrity view showing mismatch rate, reconnect frequency, p99 token latency.
- Telemetry: collect segment checksums and epoch when feature-flagged to validate shim effectiveness.
postmortem_notes:
- Initial delay: incident was customer-reported and not caught by unit tests; add disconnect chaos to CI.
- Communication: customer support handled targeted outreach correctly, but SLA documentation needs a short note on resume best practices.
- Learnings: engineering must treat segmenting + KV cache boundaries as a single atomic space for resume semantics.
- Follow-ups: schedule a cross-team retrofit session with Serving Runtime, Orchestration, and SDK teams to align on resume semantics and client-side helpers.
